Budget 2027: Rising wave of protests

cards.what_happened: Parliament is debating Budget 2027 while trade unions and state workers protest against it. The Opposition, including former Minister Prof. G. L. Peiris, says the budget fails to address unemployment, living costs, and welfare. The government defends its budget and claims it rebuilt the economy, but critics warn of slower growth and higher inflation.
details: Government doctors have threatened trade union action over their grievances, and nurses, public sector engineers, teachers, principals, university academics, non-academic workers, and Development Officers are also protesting. The government won elections by promising to grant pay hikes twice a year, and the JVP-led NPP secured nearly four-fifths of the postal votes at the 2024 parliamentary election, compared with 61.56% of the overall vote. Government leaders have boasted of overflowing coffers.

Former Minister Prof. G. L. Peiris is among those leading the Opposition's campaign against Budget 2027. Speaking at the People's United Opposition political office on Flower Road, Colombo, on Tuesday, he said the budget lacks a practical programme to address unemployment, rising living costs, and declining welfare. He noted that unemployment among educated youth stood at 43%, with approximately 40,000 graduates unable to find jobs, and that nearly half of those unable to secure employment were compelled to seek jobs overseas, while the departure of doctors created approximately 7,000 vacancies in the medical sector and universities have only 6,000 teachers against a requirement of 12,000.

The Opposition says the government has failed to utilise the funds allocated for development, citing a World Bank report that only 16.4% of capital expenditure allocated in last year's Budget had been utilised by September this year, with pending use by year-end expected to reach only 30% to 40% of the allocation. It argues that employment generation requires capital investment to revitalise the economy, attract foreign direct investment, and generate jobs. Ruling party members, however, describe the budget as a magic wand and say the public must exercise patience.

Prof. Peiris compared economic growth of 5% in 2024 with a slowdown from 5.1% in the second quarter of 2025 to 4.2% in the corresponding period this year. He said inflation had risen from 0.8% to 8.3%, while the dollar had climbed from Rs. 293 to Rs. 337. He added that foreign reserves had risen by US$6 billion under Wickremesinghe, compared with about US$1 billion under the present government, and Cabinet Spokesman Dr Nalinda Jayatissa said Wickremesinghe made 33 foreign trips costing Rs. 1,010 million while President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spent Rs. 31.7 million on eight foreign trips, with 421 individuals accompanying Wickremesinghe from his visit to the United Kingdom on September 17, 2022, to his tour of India on June 8, 2024.
key_facts: Parliament debates Budget 2027 amid trade union and state worker protests.
Government doctors, nurses, teachers, engineers, and university staff demand relief.
The NPP won nearly four-fifths of postal votes in the 2024 election, compared with 61.56% overall.
Prof. G. L. Peiris says the budget ignores unemployment and living costs.
Educated youth unemployment is 43%, with 40,000 graduates jobless.
Only 16.4% of last year's capital budget was used by September.
Growth fell from 5.1% to 4.2%; inflation rose to 8.3%.
Wickremesinghe made 33 foreign trips costing Rs. 1,010 million.
cards.whats_next: Industrial action is likely to snowball, threatening economic and political stability. The government should abandon confrontation and negotiate with the trade unions.
cards.blurb: Doctors, teachers, and engineers protest Budget 2027 as the Opposition attacks the government's economic record.
cards.spoken: Welcome. Parliament is debating Budget 2027 as trade unions and state workers protest. Government doctors have threatened industrial action, and nurses, teachers, engineers, and university staff are also demanding relief. The Opposition says the budget does nothing practical for unemployment, rising living costs, or welfare. Former Minister Prof. G. L. Peiris said 43 percent of educated youth are unemployed and about 40,000 graduates cannot find work. The government, however, calls its budget a magic wand and asks the public to be patient. It also claims it inherited a bankrupt economy, though critics point to slower growth, higher inflation, and the dollar climbing from 293 rupees to 337 rupees. A minister revealed that former President Ranil Wickremesinghe made thirty-three foreign trips costing over one billion rupees, while President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spent far less on eight trips. It warns unrest could snowball unless the government negotiates with the unions.
